The Long-Term Care Financial Checklist

What to gather about Mom's income, accounts, insurance and care bills.

Download PDF

Mom's care bills have started arriving, and her paperwork has never been in one place. Before anyone tries to work out what it all comes to, make sure you have these in hand. Check what you've found. Anything unchecked is something still to look for, not a verdict about Mom or about your family.

Gather

Write down

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you gather and notice. It doesn't add anything up, say what any account or policy means for paying for Mom's care, or tell you what to do with it. Rules vary by state, and nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice. Those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional, and to the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You've gathered what you could, and you can see what hasn't turned up yet. The planning interview takes it from there: it asks about your family's situation, one question at a time, and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for Mom's care.

Get Your Free Planning Report ›

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 or 2 follow the lists of financial records that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and AARP suggest keeping together. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
